transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-12
Time: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (CEO), Devon Carter (CTO), Priya Nair (VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (Head of Product), Sofia Ramirez (Head of People), Ethan Zhou (Director of Sales) + all-hands distribution list

Summary:
Maya kicked off with a high-level Q4 wrap, some numbers on ARR and Dedicated momentum. Devon covered performance wins and a short post-mortem on an incident in late December. Priya and Liam walked through product priorities for Q1, and Sofia covered hiring cadence. The call ended with explicit next steps and action items.

-- Transcript body (automated transcription, occasional mis-hears) --
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, uh welcome to the January all hands, um happy new year, thanks for joining, we've got a packed agenda, we'll keep it to about 45ish minutes and then open Q&A.
[00:00:22] Devon: Quick shout out to infra for the December push, the Dedicated autoscale change cut tail latency by about 18 percent, that was huge, uh big props.
[00:00:45] Priya: Yeah and the batching improvements plus the KV prefix caching that we rolled are doing the heavy lifting, some of the numbers are in the deck, please check the S3 link, I think there's a small typo on slide 6, it says 1.2 M but should be 1.12 M.
[00:01:10] Liam: On product, we're shipping the new model routing policy controls this quarter, the feature lets customers prefer low-cost variants during non-critical windows, and fallback tiers for availability.
[00:01:36] Ethan: From sales, Enterprise inbound is faster than expected — we've closed three Dedicated deals in DEC and one Private in early Jan, pipeline looks healthy. We need to tighten our onboarding and security doc bundle.
[00:02:05] Sofia: Hiring update: we're prioritizing two senior infra roles and a product manager, interview loops are being streamlined to two loops instead of three to cut time-to-offer.
[00:02:28] Maya: Great, let's go into the incident briefly — Devon?
[00:02:34] Devon: Sure, um on Dec 28 we had a partial degradation in one region, root cause turned out to be a kernel selection regression after a rollout, the quick summary: certain models on xpu nodes fell back to a less optimal kernel which caused CPU serialization in the dispatcher. We rolled back the rollout and patched the selector.
[00:03:05] Devon: The post-mortem is in Confluence, link in the chat, but action items include tighter rollout checks, more canary traffic and a perf benchmark before merge. There was some noise in the logs that the guardrails missed — we'll add a tracer and an alert on kernel mismatch rate.
[00:03:38] Priya: On the reliability roadmap we're adding two things: a targeted canary job per-pool and a new perf swarm that runs at scale nightly, that should catch regressions earlier.
[00:04:02] Maya: Questions?
[00:04:10] (silence, some murmurs)
[00:04:22] Anonymous: Quick question, are we going to slow down releases to avoid incidents?
[00:04:28] Devon: Not slow down, but tighter guardrails; canaries and more staging traffic, plus a hitless rollback path.
[00:04:46] Liam: On product priorities: three focus areas for Q1 — 1) Improve latency SLOs for short-chat workloads, 2) Expand Optimize recommendations for caching and quantization, 3) Improve private deployment onboarding (VPC templates and KMS docs).
[00:05:14] Priya: For the latency SLOs we're experimenting with sequence-length aware batching and a new kernel schedule; early tests show 12-15% token latency improvements for 1-2 token completions.
[00:05:42] Devon: Also we have a follow-up internal doc on model quantization tradeoffs — the short version is 4-bit layouts ok for many workloads but we need to measure p95 behavior.
[00:06:05] Ethan: On sales ops, please make sure the SOC 2 and ISO docs are easy to find, customers ask during POC all the time — we lost one deal because the security appendix wasn't clear.
[00:06:27] Sofia: We're going to centralize the compliance artifacts and link from the sales playbook, that'll be done by next week.
[00:06:38] Maya: Okay financials quick — Q4 closed up at 1.12M ARR net new, rollout of Dedicated continues to be our biggest driver, gross margin is improving cuz of batching and caching.
[00:06:57] (someone coughs)
[00:07:04] Maya: We're also trimming a few low ROI experiments and redirecting resources to core infra and product.
[00:07:15] Priya: On hiring and org — we've consolidated the runtime and infra teams under one lead to improve kernel dev velocity, that'll reduce review stuff.
[00:07:30] Devon: We also added a small team focused on kernel selection and compilation heuristics — their first deliverable is a small benchmark suite to be shared next week.
[00:07:47] Liam: Customer feedback loop — early Private customers asked for better rollout docs and a one-click VPC template, we're prioritizing that.
[00:08:05] Ethan: Sales metrics: average sales cycle for Dedicated is down 2 weeks, net new ARR velocity increased month-over-month. Need to keep momentum.
[00:08:20] Maya: Alright I want to highlight two customer stories — one fintech POC that moved to Dedicated after a successful low-latency test, and a health-care customer that picked Private because of data residency and KMS needs. Both are in the deck.
[00:08:46] Priya: For the Optimize toolkit, we implemented automatic suggestion flows that propose cache configs and quantization settings; initial runs show roughly 15% cost reduction for mid-sized workloads.
[00:09:10] Devon: There's an engineering caveat — suggestions are conservative and we expose per-route sim results before applying.
[00:09:20] (chat link posted: confluence/incident-pm, s3/deck)
[00:09:35] Audience Q: What's the plan for supporting new GPUs from vendors?
[00:09:40] Devon: We're expanding kernel backends and the compilation layer to support the new vendor ABI; timeline is Q2 for early support, Q3 for full validation.
[00:09:55] Audience Q: Any headcount targets next quarter?
[00:10:00] Sofia: We're hiring 8 ICs and 2 managers across infra, product, and sales; priority is infra senior hires.
[00:10:15] Maya: Ok let's do a rapid-fire around the org — each leader drop a 30s update. Devon?
[00:10:22] Devon: Shipping perf improvements, rolling out new canary infra, kernel bench next week.
[00:10:38] Priya: Roadmap milestones for q1: model routing GA, optimize v1, private onboarding docs.
[00:10:52] Liam: New customer-facing templates for VPC and KMS, and a streamlined POC checklist.
[00:11:05] Ethan: Sales piloting a new pricing tier for mid-market to increase adoption of Dedicated.
[00:11:18] Sofia: Hiring and onboarding improvements, faster offers, better scorecards.
[00:11:30] (short pause)
[00:11:36] Maya: Alright closing notes — watch the deck, contribute to the post-mortem doc if you have context, and thanks for the hard work. We'll open up for Q&A for the remaining time.
[00:11:50] Q: Can you share the Dedicated pricing tiers sooner?
[00:11:54] Ethan: I'll share an initial draft by Friday, and we'll iterate with finance and product.
[00:12:05] Q: Any update on Expand sales playbook for partners?
[00:12:10] Maya: We are evaluating two partner channels for APAC, partner playbook will be part of the Q1 partner rollout.
[00:12:22] (several people unmuting)
[00:12:35] Audience: Quick shout: the infra doc link 404s for some folks.
[00:12:40] Priya: Thanks, will fix link and re-post.
[00:12:47] (longer Q&A, interleaved comments — transcript abridged for brevity)
[00:22:00] Audience: Are we going to pressure test our price/cost math for Optimize suggestions?
[00:22:12] Devon: Yes, perf/econ team will run sensitivity analysis, and we'll publish a sanity-check table in the deck.
[00:23:10] Maya: Final callouts — customer success to prioritize SOC2 notes, sales to get Dedicated pricing out, eng to finalize KV cache tuning doc. We'll reconvene in two weeks for a reliability deep dive.
[00:23:35] Maya: Thank you all, meeting adjourned.

Post-meeting notes: Links posted in chat: confluence/postmortem-dec28, s3/q4-deck, s3/q1-roadmap. Action items and next steps recorded in the agenda doc.
